quest.title: Seven-Hued Ruins
quest.description: With Citlali's assistance, you find the ruins left behind by the Battle of Seven Colors. However, the truth that awaits your discovery is far beyond your expectations...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x49200, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act III
chapter.title: The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place we decided to meet yesterday.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who knows if Citlali will show up on time... She drank so much last night, she might not even be up yet...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ahem...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No need to sound so surprised... Drinking is just a way to pass the time. I mastered the art of moderation long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Last night doesn't count... It was a minor slip up, that's all. Anyway, I gave everything a lot of thought, and I think you're right about something.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The Battle of Seven Colors holds the key to a lot of the answers I've been searching for.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that's why you're here so early...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Great Shaman, sorry to keep you waiting. Shall we head out?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Just follow me. I'll confirm the location myself.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Of course.

talks.objective: Go to the ruined site of the battlefield

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This should be it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the battlefield is inside this place...

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: That could explain a lot of our academic questions...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Don't lose focus. Once we get to the actual site of the battle, all the evidence needed for publication will be at our fingertips.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Everyone ready?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go!

talks.objective: Enter the ruins of the Battle of Seven Colors
Enter the ruins of the Battle of Seven Colors

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, the Abyss invaded through a cave like this?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: When the Abyss first began to corrode the Ley Lines, they took every opening they could get.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: All the items here should be useful for our research...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're not to touch a single one without my nod of approval.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I don't support invasive excavation techniques, either...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: ...Ah, of course. I'll defer to the experts on this matter. Well, shall we continue?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: There are weapons here from every tribe in Natlan. The battle must have encompassed the entire nation.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Hm, sounds like we're getting closer to what the legend describes.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: But, all we can really say is that a battle took place here. There's still no evidence of any colors or some elaborate maze.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're really invested in the Battle of Seven Colors...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Haha... Well, it's the reason I came to Natlan in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Grudoc, send some of your men to search the area. We might miss something all grouped together like this. I'd like to cover all our bases.

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: All the bases? You got it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't jump to conclusions — of course this isn't the site of the actual battle. We have to keep going.

talks.objective: Analyze the mechanisms in the ruins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, we passed straight through! What was that? Some kind of color magic?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's very close to the technique Huitzilin might have used.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: That's it? Doesn't quite compare to the scale described in the legend.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Still, what a terrific archaeological find!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Enough chit-chat. We should keep going — the deeper we go, the more we'll find.

talks.objective: Continue going deeper into the ruins

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what was that? What is this place?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Look! A maze made of colors!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: It's real... I can't believe it.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on, the quality of this space... This isn't reality. It's a realm of memory!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this the Night Kingdom?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, this is a space constructed using memories as a medium. The principle is similar, but the two are not the same.
Correct!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huitzilin!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...No, it's just a trace of her consciousness left behind after creating this space.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Friends, this is my question to you — what is our strongest weapon against the Abyss? In my opinion, it's "memory."

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: After all, is it not after losing the capacity for memory, love, and compassion that our enemies fell to the Abyss?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: That is why, with our memories, we possess a power the Abyss cannot hope to match.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: I have discovered the perfect medium for us to wield that weapon. You know it as "color."

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: The more cherished the memory, the more vivid its color. As memories disappear, their color fades first. That is why color is the best vehicle to wield the power of memory.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Guided by vibrant colors, your capacity for memory is what will allow you to navigate this maze.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Without that capacity, enemies will fail to cross the barrier in front of them and be trapped here for eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: So, be brave, my friends, and march forward!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any ideas, Citlali?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hmph, sounds like she left a tutorial. Not surprising, she always did have to hand-hold her talentless students... Follow me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're out... Looks like we made it through the maze.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hold on, this is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, so pretty! The thing inside the sphere looks exactly like the maze!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's like a miniature blueprint made from a special dye.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: That color...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The dye was modified using a secret technique to harness the power of memories and create mazes like the one we just witnessed.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Without that power, it's just a normal dye. But, the color it produces is still quite rare.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I would say this is the most direct evidence that the Battle of Seven Colors actually took place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The expert has spoken!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Perhaps I could take a closer look? It's an important piece of physical evidence, after all...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: No, you may not.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Grudoc suddenly charges towards the sphere, but you manage to block him with your sword.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you doing!?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #You noticed my signal... Not bad, {NICKNAME}. We make a good team.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: *scoff*... So, you've been watching me?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: A self-proclaimed book merchant who's never heard of "Shogun Almighty: Reborn as Raiden With Unlimited Power"? Please, that work was a commercial success across Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I knew you were fishy, but I didn't expect you to pull something like this.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Monsieur Montluson, we just need a few pictures for our research, not the artifact itself! What if it gets damaged or destroyed!?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Shut it! I couldn't care less about preserving this piece of trash. I would destroy it right now if I could!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, then there would be no evidence to prove the battle took place!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: What if that was my goal all along?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Hmph, pretending to be a book merchant, pretending to promote the history of Natlan and its heroes... was the only way to get information out of the people in this tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: But, make no mistake — I'm no lowly merchant. I am the future owner of the largest printing company in all of Teyvat!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: But, the dye in that sphere ruined all my plans before they could even get off the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: We've received a report that your advertisement in the paper makes false claims. Fontaine law demands it be taken down immediately.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: False claims? The dye I advertised is an unprecedented innovation! It produces colors of unmatched radiance!

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, its qualities are neither "unprecedented" nor "unmatched." According to the lady who made the report, she saw a woven scroll in Natlan made with a similar dye.

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: Even more miraculous, that substance dates back hundreds of years.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: How!? Creating this dye is the culmination of my entire life's work! You're telling me I'm hundreds of years too late!?

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: Calm down, sir...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Sorry, it's just... I know this product will be a hit. The economic boost to Fontaine will be huge! We just need to advertise it as written.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Fontaine's publishing industry is one of the best in the world. All we need to do is publish something in the paper, and all of Teyvat will think it was our invention first!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: We don't need to worry about more reports. Fontaine is far more advanced than Natlan — no one will believe such an innovative product could come from a place like that.

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: That... That goes against all of Fontaine's advertisement regulations! We can't do that!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: What if... I give you a portion of the profits? All you have to do is let the advertisement stay.

dialogues.speaker: Otila
dialogues.text: You're trying to bribe me? Careful, I'm dangerously close to reporting this to Monsieur Neuvillette.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: *frustrated grumble*...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: I knew, if I was just allowed to market my product, it would be a hit — a bestseller, even! I would be a giant in the printing industry!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: But now, no one will see it as anything more than a... poor imitation marketed centuries too late. No matter how good the product actually is, not a single one will sell.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: *scoff* I will never accept that someone from this backwards, ignorant nation could come up with that dye. Not two hundred years before me!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even when the truth is right in front of you?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: *scoff* "Truth" is in the eye of the beholder. I'm already in the printing industry — I can go into publishing no problem.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: All I have to do is destroy this sphere, write a detailed report about my findings, and publish it around the world. Then, the so-called "truth" becomes your word against mine.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Once my report is accepted as "fact," no one can accuse me of making "false claims."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's awful! What happened to "restoring the truth of history"!?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Haha, that plan hasn't changed! I will continue to spread MY truth for all of Teyvat to see!

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Ah, you mean a hero of Natlan who's not actually from Natlan? And a great shaman who, according to rumor, abandoned her tribe long ago?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: From a practical perspective, there's no reason for either of you to stand against me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Shows what you know!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Since you like rumors so much, have you heard the one about what happens to people who get on my bad side?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Ah, the wrath of Granny Itztli... Like I said, our interests aren't at odds.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: I knew from the beginning that you would accept my invitation, considering Huitzilin was your rival.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: You've lived longer than her, you're far stronger than her... And yet, she has always been more revered than you. Now, that can change.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: With the backing of the printing industry, I can take any book and send it to all four corners of Teyvat. This part of Natlan's history will be mine to tell.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: And in my version, I can erase the Battle of Seven Colors. You can be the one to have all the glory!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: That's not real history.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: That's a no, then? *scoff* Your history means nothing to me. But, it's not allowed to stand in the way of my Mora!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Done running your mouth? Good... Before handing you over to the tribe, I think I'll have my way with you first.

response.speaker: Grudoc
response.text: If this comes to a fight, per my contract, you're gonna have to go through me.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: That's right! I didn't pay all that Mora for nothing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, aren't you subordinates of The Captain? Why are you helping someone who wants to erase Natlan's history!?

response.speaker: Grudoc
response.text: The Captain? You actually bought that?

response.speaker: Grudoc
response.text: United in the pursuit of Mora, we travel the land to collect debts. Our loyalty is to Regrator, his interests, and his wealth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Regrator!?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Haha, The Captain means nothing to them. They serve a different Harbinger altogether, Regrator!

response.speaker: Grudoc
response.text: This man has the potential to become a giant in the printing industry and disrupt Fontaine's economic system. This aligns with Regrator's interests.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's all been a lie, from the very beginning!

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I don't care who you serve. When it comes to punishment, I don't discriminate.

choices.text: Just one more guy to beat up.
But, did you forget who you're talking to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, that's what you get for messing with the Hero of Natlan and Granny Itztli! They could give Regrator a run for his Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: *cough*... When did this person get so strong? Looks like the men following The Captain failed to update us on the latest intelligence...

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Not good... This is becoming more trouble than it's worth. You're on your own.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Hey! What about our contract? Your boss signed it himself!

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Our boss never signs a contract without loopholes. Even a veteran businessman like yourself fell into his trap... That's what makes him the best.

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Go home and read the fine print... All I did was trigger the exculpatory clause.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: The other stipulations have been fulfilled. I set up explosives around the cave, strong enough to destroy this place — as instructed.

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Oh, and for security purposes, all explosives have been rigged to blow at a specific time. Shouldn't be too long now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? This whole place is gonna collapse?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: You were supposed to wait until I made it out! Are you trying to kill me?

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: That depends on how fast you can run! I'm off... Ugh!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #You think you can just waltz out of here? {NICKNAME}, stop them, and then we'll make a break for it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Can do!

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Hmph, if I'm caught, I implicate my boss. Time for the backup plan...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Wait... Don't!

talks.objective: Discuss what to do with Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are we? Back in the maze? Our surroundings look different, though... What did that Fatui guy do?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good point... She'll know how to get out of here. Let's hurry — if we don't make it out before the cave collapses, we might never be able to leave!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where could she be?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's see... Citlali!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Looks like it's not gonna be that easy... What should we do?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The special color? The one you saw on that woven scroll? Why would it appear around here...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's no time to think about that.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You're right... Lead the way, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: It seems to be guiding me.
She's probably somewhere around here, too.

talks.objective: Find a way to make a breakthrough

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He triggered it just like that!? If the technique isn't activated correctly...
Instead of a realm of memory, the subjects in question will be trapped in a temporary space like this.
If you cannot escape in time, it's mutually assured destruction. But, I can't fault someone for using it as a last resort.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Hmph, I knew it. Someone of your skill wouldn't leave behind memory fragments just to parrot instructions. You must have the capacity for conscious thought...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: I appreciate the compliment. It's been a long time, my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: This is no time for a reunion. The cave outside is about to collapse. I know time flows differently in this place, but that still doesn't leave us much time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Can you help me get out?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: You misunderstand, Citlali... I'm nothing more than a fragment of memory. There's not much I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What do you mean? This space can be manipulated, right? The exit of your maze... I remember its structure. If I create an exit here, I can leave.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...You just need to tell me how to manipulate this space.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: The maze you saw earlier was constructed using the memories of many warriors of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: When people leave deep impressions on each other, their memories form connections.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: These connections are particularly strong between comrades-in-arms.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: That is how I created my maze — the connections between the memories were my needle and thread, and the special color was my fabric.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: But, if that color is crudely combined with an isolated memory, one without connections, you get a place like this.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: This space is a combination of my color and your memories. There is no way to alter or construct anything within it.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Because there are no "connections" at your disposal.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Hmph, over two hundred years, and not a single lasting connection. This is my punishment, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Well, at the very least, you have a connection to me. Otherwise, I wouldn't be able to appear in this space.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That's only because you never gave me a moment's peace... Still, it's a shame you're not around. You said it yourself — a memory fragment can't be used to create the "connections" I need...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Citlali...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, now that I have the chance to talk to you again, I need you to give me an answer.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Your special technique... You didn't pass it on to your students. You passed it onto the rival you could never beat — me. What I want to know is... Why?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: ...So, you figured it out.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: After what I saw in the maze and everything you just told me, I'm certain the technique at the center of all this... is the same one you taught me all those years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: But, you never brought up the fact that you used it to win a battle. From your description, it might as well have been a simple color trick.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm getting the feeling you always meant for me to come here... But, if this is a foreshadowed event, I'm not happy with the narrative setup.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Citlali, ever since you learned that technique, you've been able to see a special color, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: That color is the core of the technique, but it isn't my invention. It's something I discovered in the work of our ancestors.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: More specifically, you could call it... the color of memories.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: In truth, passing on the technique is a process of using that color to "tint" another person's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Yes, the technique has the power to decide victory. But, in my opinion, the capacity to add color to someone's memories is where the true value lies.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: You are fated to live a far longer life than me, Citlali. I couldn't bear the thought of all those years existing as a blank canvas in your memory...

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: So, I wanted to leave a little color behind...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...Your color, you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: One day, you, too, will want to leave behind your color in someone else's memory. When that day comes, you will understand my decision.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: (So, if you still need time, let me choose to remember you first.)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: ...I have to get out of here. That's the only way to rescue them.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Citlali, what are you—

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I understand the true principle of this technique now. If I can't construct an exit, then I will separate this color from my memories by force!

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: But, you could lose a portion of your memories that way!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know, but my memory is just a blank canvas I've neglected for two hundred years. My friends are worth the risk...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I have to find her...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: When you entered the realm of memory I constructed, I used your memories to learn about your recent experiences. I have a feeling... you're the one who will be saved this time.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: After two hundred years, someone has appeared by your side — the kind of person I could have never anticipated.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: The Night Kingdom harbors Natlan's memories, and the Traveler's connection to that realm is incredibly strong, surpassing even the shamans who worship the Lord of the Night.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: #This means that, even without your tutelage, {F#s}he can see the "color of memories."

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: What did you say?

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: #Although {F#s}he doesn't know how to wield it, {F#s}he unknowingly left behind a trace of color in your memories.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: #That was enough to guide {M#him}{F#her} to this space. You now have a "connection" at your disposal.

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: Well, Citlali, it looks like part of this was foreshadowed, but the rest is a surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... Citlali's voice! She's just up ahead!

dialogues.speaker: Huitzilin
dialogues.text: This is goodbye, my friend. Your memories over the past two hundred years are much more than a "blank canvas"... Cherish them.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huitzilin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: ...Hold my hand!

choices.text: Let's find a way to get out of here.

talks.objective: Withdraw from the ruins of the Battle of Seven Colors
Withdraw from the ruins of the Battle of Seven Colors

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did we teleport out? Man, that place was so—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! We made it out just in time!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wonder what happened to the Fatui guy and the others...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: He was most likely trapped inside that space, just like us.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: The external structures supporting that space would have collapsed with the ruin. Unless he managed to escape, he would have been crushed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He still preferred that to being caught, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What about the Fontainians?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They were standing a bit further away, right? They probably weren't pulled into the space. Maybe they already made a run for it...

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Um... Hello...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's one of that guy's employees! Quick, restrain him!

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I—I can explain! I had no idea Montluson was such a terrible person. I couldn't stop him from running, so I stayed behind and tried to find people to help rescue you.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I'm so glad you managed to get out of there!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Either way, the guards will take you back to the tribe. You'll be their problem.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I understand...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'm not here to harp on you. I just need to know one thing — which way did he run?

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: He went that way! But, I'm not sure if you can catch up...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: That way... Hmph, unless he suddenly grows a pair of wings, I think we're okay.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Elder Tlapo and a group of iktomisaurs! They caught Montluson!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Something felt off about him yesterday, so I set a few things in motion... Looks like it's time for that foreshadowing to pay off.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: My bank balance... No! NO!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's wrong with him?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ah, that's one of the tricks Claw uses to scare people... He makes people hallucinate the thing that scares them the most.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's particularly effective on weak-minded people like him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Serves him right!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I know, it was a lot to ask, making you come all the way out here during the day...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was that a declaration? Elder Tlapo didn't appoint us to a whole other task, did he?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Forget about him for now... The iktomisaurs will make sure Montluson doesn't escape before the guards arrive. In the meantime, we have unfinished business, remember?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! The special scroll! But, the dye is buried underneath a bunch of rubble now...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Huitzilin's technique hasn't been lost at all. Come with me, I'll explain everything at my house.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Oh, and {NICKNAME}, everything you said about memory... I've finally figured out my answer.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I knew you'd want to tag along. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: I'll wait here for the tribal guards. I'm so sorry the ruin was destroyed...
